  SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT constant (configurable).
- config.local.example.php: APP_ENV default changed from 'development' to
  'production' (operators copying the example get safe settings — no
  display_errors, no debug logging).
- config.local.example.php: LOG_LEVEL default changed from 'debug' to 'error'
  (debug fills disk + may log sensitive request data).
- config.local.example.php: added SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT constant (28800 = 8h)

hardening round 10 — staged JWT HttpOnly cookie migration

STAGED JWT-TO-HTTPONLY-COOKIE MIGRATION (the last major security item):
This is a STAGED, backward-compatible migration. The JSON token response is
KEPT (SPA's localStorage auth still works). The HttpOnly cookie is ADDITIVE —
it enables a future round to fully deprecate the XSS-vulnerable localStorage
token without breaking anything.

Backend changes:
- login.php: after generating the JWT, sets it as an HttpOnly cookie via
  setcookie('ess_jwt', ...). Cookie attributes: HttpOnly=true (JS can't read
  it), Secure=(auto-detected HTTPS), SameSite=Strict (not sent on cross-site
  requests), Path=/, Expires=JWT_EXPIRY. The token is ALSO returned in the
  JSON response for backward compat.
- refresh.php: reads the token from EITHER the ess_jwt cookie OR the JSON
  body (cookie takes priority — it's the more secure path). After minting
  the new token, also refreshes the cookie.
- example.config.php requireAuth(): accepts the token from the Authorization
  header (original SPA method) OR from the ess_jwt cookie as fallback. This
  means the SPA can eventually stop sending the Authorization header and rely
  on the cookie alone.

SPA changes:
- config.ts: added credentials:'include' to ALL 4 fetch calls (tryRefreshToken,
  apiRequest, retry fetch, uploadBase64Image). This tells the browser to send
  the ess_jwt cookie with every API request.
- ess-auth.ts: added credentials:'include' to the proactiveRefresh fetch call.

What this achieves:
- The JWT is now stored in an HttpOnly cookie that JavaScript CANNOT read —
  even if an XSS attack runs arbitrary JS in the SPA, the attacker cannot
  steal the token from the cookie.
- The cookie is SameSite=Strict — it's not sent on cross-site requests,
  preventing CSRF via cookie-based auth.
- Backward compat is preserved: the SPA's existing localStorage + Authorization
  header flow continues to work. The cookie is ADDITIVE.

What remains for a future round (requires runtime testing):
- SPA: stop storing the token in localStorage (remove the XSS vector entirely)
- SPA: stop sending the Authorization header (rely on cookie alone)
- These changes need SPA runtime testing to verify the cookie is set correctly
  and sent with every request.

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Security hardening round 10 — staged JWT HttpOnly cookie migration

STAGED JWT-TO-HTTPONLY-COOKIE MIGRATION (the last major security item):
This is a STAGED, backward-compatible migration. The JSON token response is
KEPT (SPA's localStorage auth still works). The HttpOnly cookie is ADDITIVE —
it enables a future round to fully deprecate the XSS-vulnerable localStorage
token without breaking anything.

Backend changes:
- login.php: after generating the JWT, sets it as an HttpOnly cookie via
  setcookie('ess_jwt', ...). Cookie attributes: HttpOnly=true (JS can't read
  it), Secure=(auto-detected HTTPS), SameSite=Strict (not sent on cross-site
  requests), Path=/, Expires=JWT_EXPIRY. The token is ALSO returned in the
  JSON response for backward compat.
- refresh.php: reads the token from EITHER the ess_jwt cookie OR the JSON
  body (cookie takes priority — it's the more secure path). After minting
  the new token, also refreshes the cookie.
- example.config.php requireAuth(): accepts the token from the Authorization
  header (original SPA method) OR from the ess_jwt cookie as fallback. This
  means the SPA can eventually stop sending the Authorization header and rely
  on the cookie alone.

SPA changes:
- config.ts: added credentials:'include' to ALL 4 fetch calls (tryRefreshToken,
  apiRequest, retry fetch, uploadBase64Image). This tells the browser to send
  the ess_jwt cookie with every API request.
- ess-auth.ts: added credentials:'include' to the proactiveRefresh fetch call.

What this achieves:
- The JWT is now stored in an HttpOnly cookie that JavaScript CANNOT read —
  even if an XSS attack runs arbitrary JS in the SPA, the attacker cannot
  steal the token from the cookie.
- The cookie is SameSite=Strict — it's not sent on cross-site requests,
  preventing CSRF via cookie-based auth.
- Backward compat is preserved: the SPA's existing localStorage + Authorization
  header flow continues to work. The cookie is ADDITIVE.

What remains for a future round (requires runtime testing):
- SPA: stop storing the token in localStorage (remove the XSS vector entirely)
- SPA: stop sending the Authorization header (rely on cookie alone)
- These changes need SPA runtime testing to verify the cookie is set correctly
  and sent with every request.

health.php: 2 new R10 flags (jwt_httponly_cookie, spa_credentials_include).

The ess_jwt HttpOnly cookie was not being set correctly on login, causing
the '401 then success' pattern (first call fails, refresh sets cookie,
retry succeeds — or refresh fails and user is logged out).

Root causes:
1. SameSite=Strict can block the cookie on some same-site fetch scenarios.
   Changed to SameSite=Lax (still blocks cross-site POST CSRF, but allows
   same-site requests + top-level navigations).
2. Secure flag was conditional on HTTPS detection which may fail behind a
   reverse proxy. Changed to always true (the site is HTTPS-only).
3. Added SERVER_PORT==443 as a third HTTPS detection fallback (for login.php).

Applied to both login.php (sets cookie on login) and refresh.php (refreshes

  escalation (anyone could POST role=admin into ess_employee_cache).

  to the authenticated user. Was unauthenticated IDOR on any user's
  notifications.
- api/ess/designations.php: add requireAuth() + fix TypeError (was
  'echo jsonResponse(true, ...)' on a void function).
- api/ess/auto-role.php: replace shared API-key with requireAuth() +
  admin/regional_manager/hr role check. Was mass role-rewrite with
  only a leaked shared key.
- api/ess/ess-employees.php: replace shared API-key with requireAuth()
  + admin/manager role check. Was full-PII leak (Aadhaar/bank/IFSC/
  nominee) by ?id=N with only the leaked key.
- php_payroll/download_salary_template.php: add session auth +
  admin/HR/manager role check. Was unauthenticated PII leak of every
  employee code + name.
- php_payroll/modules/api/crop-save.php: add session auth + role
  check. Was unauthenticated file write to /uploads/ + employee
  record update.
- php_payroll/modules/api/expense-api.php: add session auth + role
  check AND optimise the per-request ALTER TABLE loop (11 SHOW
  COLUMNS queries -> 1, cached per-process). Was IDOR + DoS.
- php_payroll/modules/api/manager-units.php: add session auth + role
  check. Was supervisor-readable PII doc URLs for any manager's units.
- php_payroll/modules/employee/import.php: restrict to admin/HR.
  Was supervisor-accessible bulk employee import.

CONFIG HARDENING:
- api/ess/example.config.php: add runtime guard that refuses to serve
  any endpoint if JWT_SECRET/API_KEY are still the placeholders; reduce
  JWT_EXPIRY from 4 days (345600) to 24h (86400).
- .gitignore: exclude api/ess/config.php + php_payroll/config/
  config.local.php (README previously falsely claimed config.php was
  gitignored).

DATA-CORRECTNESS FIXES (status='active' -> 'approved' on employees
table; 'active' is not in the ENUM per constants.php):
- modules/compliance/dashboard.php, modules/billing/create.php,
  modules/report/esi/inspection-report.php, modules/report/mis/
  form-16.php, modules/report/mis/salary-certificate.php,
  includes/class.client.php

FEATURE:
- api/ess/health.php: extend into a security-posture endpoint.
  GET /health = basic liveness; GET /health?detail=1 = reports
  config_present, config_loadable, jwt_secret_is_placeholder,
  api_key_is_placeholder, jwt_expiry_seconds, posture_ok. No secrets
  are ever leaked — booleans only.

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Fix: cookie not setting — SameSite Strict→Lax + Secure=true always

The ess_jwt HttpOnly cookie was not being set correctly on login, causing
the '401 then success' pattern (first call fails, refresh sets cookie,
retry succeeds — or refresh fails and user is logged out).

Root causes:
1. SameSite=Strict can block the cookie on some same-site fetch scenarios.
   Changed to SameSite=Lax (still blocks cross-site POST CSRF, but allows
   same-site requests + top-level navigations).
2. Secure flag was conditional on HTTPS detection which may fail behind a
   reverse proxy. Changed to always true (the site is HTTPS-only).
3. Added SERVER_PORT==443 as a third HTTPS detection fallback (for login.php).

Applied to both login.php (sets cookie on login) and refresh.php (refreshes
cookie on token renewal)." class="Link--secondary" href="/rcstrue/RCS_HRMS/commit/f3b091a51e6ce7b4aafef8efaa0c3a40de60feea">Fix: cookie not setting — SameSite Strict→Lax + Secure=true   only a leaked shared key.
- api/ess/ess-employees.php: replace shared API-key with requireAuth()
  + admin/manager role check. Was full-PII leak (Aadhaar/bank/IFSC/
  nominee) by ?id=N with only the leaked key.
- php_payroll/download_salary_template.php: add session auth +
  admin/HR/manager role check. Was unauthenticated PII leak of every
  employee code + name.
- php_payroll/modules/api/crop-save.php: add session auth + role
  check. Was unauthenticated file write to /uploads/ + employee
  record update.
- php_payroll/modules/api/expense-api.php: add session auth + role
  check AND optimise the per-request ALTER TABLE loop (11 SHOW
  COLUMNS queries -> 1, cached per-process). Was IDOR + DoS.
- php_payroll/modules/api/manager-units.php: add session auth + role
  check. Was supervisor-readable PII doc URLs for any manager's units.
- php_payroll/modules/employee/import.php: restrict to admin/HR.
  Was supervisor-accessible bulk employee import.

CONFIG HARDENING:
- api/ess/example.config.php: add runtime guard that refuses to serve
  any endpoint if JWT_SECRET/API_KEY are still the placeholders; reduce
  JWT_EXPIRY from 4 days (345600) to 24h (86400).
- .gitignore: exclude api/ess/config.php + php_payroll/config/
  config.local.php (README previously falsely claimed config.php was
  gitignored).

DATA-CORRECTNESS FIXES (status='active' -> 'approved' on employees
table; 'active' is not in the ENUM per constants.php):
- modules/compliance/dashboard.php, modules/billing/create.php,

  form-16.php, modules/report/mis/salary-certificate.php,
  includes/class.client.php

FEATURE:
- api/ess/health.php: extend into a security-posture endpoint.

  config_present, config_loadable, jwt_secret_is_placeholder,
  api_key_is_placeholder, jwt_expiry_seconds, posture_ok. No secrets
  are ever leaked — booleans only.

<ol dir="auto">
<li><code>POST /api/ess/login</code> → JWT set in HttpOnly <code>ess_jwt</code> cookie (24h expiry)</li>
<li>All subsequent requests: cookie sent automatically by browser</li>
<li>Fallback: <code>Authorization: Bearer <token></code> header (for non-browser clients)</li>
<li>When token nears expiry, client calls <code>POST /api/ess/refresh</code> (5-min grace window)</li>
<li>If refresh fails (e.g., >5 min past expiry), redirect to login</li>
</ol>

<p dir="auto">The <code>team-summary.php</code> endpoint handles multiple actions via POST body <code>action</code> field:</p>
<markdown-accessiblity-table data-catalyst=""><table>

<tr>
<th>Action</th>
<th>Description</th>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>add_temp</code></td>
<td>Add a temporary employee for a unit/month/year</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>del_temp</code></td>
<td>Remove a temporary employee</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Important notes:</strong></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>attendance_summary.source</code> is <code>ENUM('Manual','Excel Upload')</code> — do NOT insert custom source values</li>
<li><code>employee_advances</code> does NOT have <code>present</code>/<code>wo</code> columns — only <code>adv1</code>, <code>office_advance</code>, <code>dress_advance</code></li>
<li><code>employee_advances.employee_id</code> is INT type</li>
<li><code>attendance_summary.employee_id</code> is INT type</li>
<li><code>payroll.employee_id</code> is VARCHAR (stores employee_code string)</li>
<li>PHP <code>bind_param()</code> requires <strong>variables</strong> (not expressions) for pass-by-reference</li>
</ul>
